```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "Time to first payment fits the 90-day goal better. A is a low-stakes self-serve purchase at $9–$29/mo, and a customer-facing status page needs no access to the buyer's codebase. B needs pipeline and source-code access, likely a DPA and security review, and enough historical CI data to overcome cold start before it delivers value. Each step slows a first sale.",
    "A's demand evidence ties directly to willingness to pay. The r/SaaS thread on the market leader charging $399/month, together with sourced Statuspage tier pricing up to $1,499+/mo, shows a pricing pain a cheap entrant can address. B's demand evidence shows that flaky tests hurt, but not that anyone will pay for an LLM to choose which tests block a change.",
    "A cites a sourced solo-operator outcome in its own category: Instatus at about $10k MRR. B cites no monetized indie comparable. Its indie and OSS entrants (ci-sherlock-agent, flaketriage, ai-flake-sleuth, flaky-detector-agent) are described as unmonetized.",
    "B's own case against names a trust barrier that is hard to clear quickly. False negatives destroy trust, and earning that trust typically takes months of track record. A carries no comparable risk that would undo a sale.",
    "A's build-feasibility claim is reasoned from its narrow scope, though not sourced. B's 'six weeks' time-to-MVP is explicitly marked [unsourced] and so counts as missing.",
    "A is still seriously exposed. OneUptime offers a free tier, StillOnline already sells at $9/mo with an agent angle, and Hyperping already runs the 'incumbent overpriced' SEO wedge. A is chosen as the less bad first bet, not as a strong one."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B's demand evidence does not show demand for the proposed product. The lead quote comes from a Trunk TLM describing the adoption of an internal flaky-test dashboard, which is vendor-published content about a non-LLM tool. The r/programming quote praises sorting by impact and auto-ticketing, not LLM-driven selection of blocking tests. The 20.2M-CI-jobs statistic is from the same Trunk source and establishes that the problem exists, not that buyers will pay. No evidence shows any team paying for, or willing to let, an LLM gate merges.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate-to-low confidence. Both briefs describe crowded markets with free alternatives. A's acquisition picture is weak: it is effectively competing against $0, and established players already hold the SEO channel. The decision rests mainly on A's lower purchase friction and trust barrier relative to B, not on strong positive evidence that A will land a customer within 90 days."
}
```
